Risk Title: Ransomware via compromised vendor remote access
Vulnerability: Vendor remote-access accounts not required to use MFA; access never verified at onboarding
Existing Controls: Annual BAA renewal; vendor self-attestation questionnaire
Recommended Controls: Require phishing-resistant MFA for all vendor remote access; brokered/just-in-time vendor access; continuous monitoring of Critical-tier vendors

Risk Title: Prolonged outage of claims clearinghouse halts revenue and e-prescribing
Threat Source: Third-party service failure (ransomware or outage at vendor)
Vulnerability: Single clearinghouse with no tested failover; no manual downtime procedures for claims or e-prescribing
Existing Controls: Vendor SLA (no security or recovery terms)
Recommended Controls: Pre-contract a secondary clearinghouse; document and drill manual downtime procedures; maintain cash-reserve plan

Risk Title: Business Associate Agreements lack enforceable security terms
Vulnerability: BAAs contain no minimum controls, audit rights, or breach-notification SLA
Recommended Controls: Modernized BAA: MFA certification, SOC 2 Type II or HITRUST evidence, 24-hour incident notification, audit rights

Risk Title: Compromise of a vendor's subcontractor (fourth party)
Threat Source: External attacker targeting the vendor's supply chain
Vulnerability: No visibility into subcontractors used by Critical-tier vendors
Recommended Controls: Require Critical-tier vendors to disclose material subcontractors and flow down equivalent security requirements

Vulnerability: Inconsistent MFA on webmail and EHR remote access; annual-only awareness training
Existing Controls: Email spam filter; annual HIPAA training
Recommended Controls: MFA on all remote and email access; monthly phishing simulations; external-sender banners; phishing report button

Risk Title: Ransomware spreads through unpatched internal systems
Vulnerability: Patch cycle exceeds 60 days for critical vulnerabilities; flat network segments
Recommended Controls: Risk-based patching SLA (critical in 14 days); EDR on all endpoints; network segmentation of clinical systems

Risk Title: EHR data cannot be restored after a destructive attack
Vulnerability: Backups not immutable; restore never tested end-to-end
Recommended Controls: Immutable, offline-isolated backups; quarterly restore tests with documented recovery times

Risk Title: Former workforce or vendor accounts remain active
Threat Source: Former employee, contractor, or attacker using stale credentials
Vulnerability: No automated deprovisioning; vendor accounts not tied to contract end dates
Recommended Controls: Automate HR-driven deprovisioning; quarterly access reviews; vendor accounts expire with contract

Risk Title: Inappropriate employee access to patient records
Vulnerability: Audit logs collected but not proactively reviewed
Recommended Controls: Automated EHR access monitoring (e.g., VIP and coworker record alerts); sanctions policy enforcement

Risk Title: Medical devices compromised through vendor maintenance connections
Threat Source: External attacker or compromised device vendor
Vulnerability: Device vendors keep always-on remote access; devices on shared network; legacy OS on some imaging systems
Recommended Controls: Complete device inventory; segment medical devices; vendor remote access only through brokered, logged sessions

Risk Title: Controlled-substance diversion from Automated Dispensing Cabinets
Vulnerability: Override reports reviewed inconsistently; shared credentials on some units
Existing Controls: ADC badge + PIN access; monthly pharmacy reconciliation
Recommended Controls: Diversion analytics on ADC transactions; ban shared credentials; biometric ADC login

Risk Title: Hurricane or extended power loss disrupts campus and on-site data center
Vulnerability: Single on-site data center; generator fuel supply for ~72 hours
Recommended Controls: Secondary hosting site or cloud failover for EHR; fuel resupply contracts; annual hurricane tabletop exercise

Risk Title: Third-party incident not covered by incident response plan
Vulnerability: IR plan written for internal incidents only; never exercised with vendors
Recommended Controls: Add third-party incident playbook; joint tabletop with Critical-tier vendors annually

Risk Title: Lost or stolen laptop exposes PHI
Vulnerability: Full-disk encryption not enforced on all laptops
Existing Controls: Encryption on most new devices; asset tags
Recommended Controls: Enforce full-disk encryption via device management; remote wipe capability

Risk Title: Theft or loss of radioactive sealed sources
Vulnerability: Sources stored in controlled areas; inventory checks periodic
Existing Controls: Locked storage; NRC-required inventories; badge access
Recommended Controls: Maintain current NRC/state program controls; reassess annually
